```plato
//==
// # Surfaces
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Surfaces — parametric evaluation of the named surface types
//  - Derived functions for the surface, solid, and volume interfaces
//  - Deformation bodies for the control-net and sampled surfaces

library Surfaces
{
    //==
    // # Surfaces — parametric evaluation of the named surface types
    //
    // The IParametricSurface obligations (Eval / ClosedU / ClosedV) for the types
    // declared in `surfaces.types.plato`, `surfaces.types.plato`, and
    // `surfaces.types.plato`. Same UV convention as `library Solids` in
    // solids.library.plato: UV is the unit square, U is the first (profile / column)
    // direction and V the second (sweep / row) direction, and ClosedU/ClosedV say
    // whether the surface seams shut across that direction — which is exactly the
    // pair `AllQuadFaceIndices(nCols, nRows, ClosedU, ClosedV)` in
    // meshes.library.plato consumes.
    //
    // Every surface now evaluates. Two of them carry a documented approximation:
    //
    //   * The sweeps (SweptSurface, TubeSurface) use a FIXED-UP frame — the tangent
    //     plus a deterministically chosen perpendicular — not the rotation-minimizing
    //     frame the type doc names. A rotation-minimizing frame is defined by
    //     integrating along the path, which is sequential state this vocabulary has no
    //     way to carry; the fixed-up frame agrees with it wherever the path does not
    //     turn about its own tangent, and twists relative to it where it does.
    //   * OffsetSurface reads its base normal from central differences of
    //     `Base.Eval`, because `IParametricSurface` exposes no derivative (only
    //     `IDifferentiableSurface` does). Exact for a surface whose base IS
    //     differentiable; noisy near a seam or a degenerate parameterization.
    //
    // Both are noted at their bodies. The worklist entry is plato-321.

    //==
    // Shared helpers

    // A unit vector orthogonal to v, chosen deterministically: crossing against
    // whichever canonical axis v is least aligned with, so the product is never
    // degenerate. Precondition: v is non-zero.
    AnyPerpendicular(v: Vector3D): Vector3D {
        var axis = v.X.Abs <= v.Y.Abs && v.X.Abs <= v.Z.Abs
            ? Vector3D.UnitX
            : (v.Y.Abs <= v.Z.Abs ? Vector3D(0.0, 1.0, 0.0) : Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0));
        return v.Cross(axis).Normalize;
    }
```
